claim: CommandResponseFromHTTPBody only routes to CommandResponseFromJSON (and thus IsValid) when Content-Type is exactly application/json; every other content type, including an absent one, falls to CommandResponseFromPlainText which never validates, so the third party being constrained picks the branch and bypasses the new gate.
raw: #1 🟠 High: The new validation is bypassable by a single response header — the plain-text branch is never validated

claim: IsValid recurses into ExtraResponses and returns on first failure, so one invalid nested extra_responses entry now rejects the whole payload at parse time: previously CreateCommandPost silently dropped the bad extra while the main post succeeded, now neither the main post nor any extra is created and the caller gets HTTP 500.
raw: #2 🟠 High: One invalid nested `extra_responses` entry now fails the whole response — a partial success becomes a total failure with no posts and an HTTP 500

claim: Validation is applied on the read side only: api4/command.go encodes the CommandResponse with no validation while Client4.ExecuteCommand parses it via CommandResponseFromJSON which now hard-fails, so the server can emit responses its own client rejects after the post side effect has already happened.
raw: #3 🟠 High: Validation is applied on the read side only — the server can emit responses that its own `Client4` now rejects

claim: The hardcoded 65535-byte cap contradicts the deployment-configurable rune-based post size limit derived by determineMaxPostSize; on deployments with an enlarged posts.message column, text that Post.IsValid would accept is rejected by this fixed byte constant that no configuration can raise.
raw: #4 🟠 High: Hardcoded 65535-**byte** cap contradicts the deployment-configurable, rune-based post size limit

claim: The local `maxLength := 65535` restates the literal value of PostMessageMaxBytesV2 declared in the same package at post.go:72, so the two can silently diverge; every other length limit in this package is an exported constant.
raw: #5 🟡 Medium: `maxLength := 65535` silently duplicates `PostMessageMaxBytesV2` from the same package

claim: Neither model.command_response.is_valid.response_type.app_error nor model.command_response.is_valid.text.app_error exists in server/i18n/en.json, so the untranslated key string is returned verbatim into logs, the AppError chain, and Go API consumers' error strings; CI does not catch referenced-but-absent IDs.
raw: #6 🟡 Medium: Both new error IDs are missing from `server/i18n/en.json`, so the untranslated key string is what reaches logs and API consumers

claim: IsValid recurses to unlimited depth while both consumers (HandleCommandResponse and the attachment stringification loop) process only one level of extra_responses, so a bogus response_type at the second level — content the server would discard unread — now fails the entire command.
raw: #7 🟡 Medium: `IsValid` recurses to unlimited depth, but the consumer only ever processes one level of `extra_responses`

claim: The new tests leave the accepting boundary unguarded (mutating > to >= at command_response.go:86 broke no test; no case at exactly 65535), assert no error identity (bare assert.Error, no AppError.Id check), never test IsValid directly or beyond one nesting level, never cover the resp == nil guard, and never cover CommandResponseFromHTTPBody's plain-text bypass.
raw: #8 🟡 Medium: The new validation's tests leave the accepting boundary and the error identity unpinned

claim: CommandResponseFromJSON in the separately tagged public Go module now rejects payloads it previously accepted, changing the observable contract of an exported function with no deprecation path and no `#### Release Note` block, which the root AGENTS.md requires for API or breaking changes.
raw: #9 🟡 Medium: Breaking behavior change to a released public Go module, undocumented

claim: The recursive validation propagates the nested error verbatim with the same `CommandResponse.IsValid` where-string at every depth, so a caller cannot tell which extra_responses entry failed; the package convention (message_attachment.go:104-106) wraps with positional index context.
raw: #10 🟢 Low: Recursive validation returns the nested error verbatim, so the caller cannot tell which entry failed

claim: The length error passes nil params, unlike sibling validators (Post.IsValid passes Length and MaxLength, TermsOfService.IsValid passes MaxLength), so the translated message cannot state the limit that was exceeded.
raw: #11 🟢 Low: The length error carries no `MaxLength` param, unlike every sibling validator

claim: IsValid sets http.StatusBadRequest but the caller wraps every error from CommandResponseFromHTTPBody with a hardcoded http.StatusInternalServerError and AppError.Wrap never copies the wrapped status, so third-party payload faults are reported as HTTP 500 Mattermost server faults.
raw: P1 🟡 Medium: `http.StatusBadRequest` is discarded on the slash-command path; third-party faults are reported as HTTP 500

claim: ExtraResponses has no count bound: each entry becomes a separate post insert or ephemeral broadcast, so a single 300 KB webhook body can demand on the order of 10^4 post creations, and the new recursive validator is the natural place to bound this but does not.
raw: P2 🟡 Medium: `ExtraResponses` has no count bound, and the new recursive validator is the natural place for one

claim: The `// check response type` comment merely restates the next line, while the genuinely non-obvious decisions in the function (why "" is accepted, why 65535, why reject rather than degrade) are undocumented.
raw: `server/public/model/command_response.go:80` — the `// check response type` comment restates the next line

claim: Stack exhaustion via deeply nested extra_responses — considered and refuted by probe: 1000 and 4000 levels validate cleanly and 6000 is rejected by encoding/json's maxNestingDepth before IsValid runs; only the explicitness of the recursion bound is at issue.
raw: Stack exhaustion via deeply nested `extra_responses`

claim: Typed-nil *AppError boxed as a non-nil error — considered and dismissed: at both assignment points (:72 and :95) err is declared as the concrete *AppError via := and the nil check happens before any interface conversion.
raw: Typed-nil `*AppError` boxed as a non-nil `error`

claim: Empty response_type wrongly rejected — considered and refuted by probe: {"text":"hi"} is accepted, so the `!= ""` clause is correct.
raw: Empty `response_type` wrongly rejected

claim: nil entries in extra_responses causing a panic — considered and refuted by probe: {"text":"hi","extra_responses":[null]} is accepted and the resp == nil guard at :91 works, though it is untested.

claim: The "wrong unit" half of the byte-vs-rune claim was judged weak: PostMessageMaxBytesV2 = 65535 is the byte-based storage ground truth and PostMessageMaxRunesV2 is derived from it, so a byte check is defensible in isolation.
raw: "Wrong unit" half of the byte-vs-rune claim

claim: t.Parallel() with the testCase loop variable — considered and dismissed: server/public/go.mod declares Go 1.26.3, so per-iteration loop variables apply.
